title: Why the Cowboy Who Draws First Loses #shorts
sources: University of Birmingham news release, 'The quick and the dead' (3 Feb 2010), and EurekAlert / BBSRC release: Niels Bohr suggested the gunslinger who draws second is faster because he reacts; Andrew Welchman's team ran 'laboratory gunfights' with rows of buttons instead of guns; reacting participants moved on average 21 milliseconds faster; Bohr reportedly tested his idea in toy-pistol duels with George Gamow and won every time; 'probably just a very good shot'

National Geographic (Ed Yong, 2 Feb 2010), 'Why does the gunslinger who draws first always get shot?': reactors executed the movement about 10% faster (21 ms), but that benefit was overwhelmed by the roughly 200 milliseconds it took to react in the first place, so reactors very rarely beat initiators; Bohr's wins were anecdotal
Welchman et al. 2010, 'The quick and the dead: when reaction beats intention', Proceedings of the Royal Society B, doi:10.1098/rspb.2009.2123
